blogs.title: A First-Timer's Guide to Hiking Europe's Stunning Alpine Lakes
blogs.summary: How to plan routes, pack layers and pick the best season for your first alpine lake hike.

thumbnail.alt: Traveller reading a map beside a mountain lake

children.text: Why start with a lake hike

Alpine lake trails are the friendliest way into mountain hiking. Most follow well-marked paths with gentle climbs, and the reward at the top is a mirror of turquoise water framed by snowy peaks. You get big views without technical skills or special gear.
What to pack for the trail
A breathable base layer and a light insulating jacket for the summit
A waterproof shell, since mountain weather can change within minutes
Broken-in hiking boots with good grip and a spare pair of socks
Snacks, two litres of water and a small first aid kit
Choose the right season

Late June to mid-September brings open trails, warm afternoons and wildflowers around most alpine lakes. Snow can linger on higher passes well into July, so check local trail reports and hut websites before you set off.

Start early in the morning whatever the month. Afternoon thunderstorms are common in summer, the light on the water is softer at sunrise, and you will have the lakeshore almost to yourself before the cable cars open.

imagePairLeft.alt: Snow-capped Swiss Alps above a green valley

imagePairRight.alt: Alpine chalets and a wildflower meadow below a snowy peak

children.text: Start with a classic loop
Pick a well-marked loop under twelve kilometres for your first hike. You will have time to stop for photos, picnics and a cold dip without racing the sunset back down to the village and your car.

Good first choices include the Oeschinensee trail above Kandersteg in Switzerland, the Lago di Sorapis path in the Italian Dolomites and the gentle circuit around Lake Bled in Slovenia. Each one offers bright turquoise water, clear signs and a mountain hut for lunch on the terrace.

wideImage.alt: Snow-capped peaks reflected in a still mountain lake

children.text: Staying safe in the mountains

Tell someone where you are going and when you expect to return, even on a popular trail. Download an offline map before you leave the valley, because phone signal often disappears behind the first ridge.
Turn back if the weather changes or the path becomes harder than expected. The lake will still be there next summer, and knowing when to stop is the most important skill any new hiker can learn.
Your first summit
Your first alpine lake hike will not be your last. Once you breathe the mountain air and see that turquoise water, you will be planning the next trail before reaching the car park.

blogs.title: Slow Travel: How to Truly Unwind on Your Next Beach Holiday
blogs.summary: Swap packed itineraries for long mornings, local food and real rest on your next beach escape.

thumbnail.alt: Traveller in a sun hat relaxing on a deck chair by the sea

children.text: What slow travel means

Slow travel is about staying longer in fewer places and letting each day unfold at its own pace. Instead of ticking off sights, you settle into one beach town, learn the names of the local cafe owners and come home feeling genuinely rested.
Choose the right base
A small town with a walkable beach and a morning market
A guesthouse or villa with a kitchen and a shaded terrace
Easy boat or bus links for one or two day trips
Quiet evenings, with a few good restaurants close to the sea
Stay longer in one place

Basing yourself in a single beach town for a week means fewer transfers and more time to settle into a gentle routine. You unpack once, learn the best swimming spots and quickly start to feel like a local.

Long stays often unlock better rates too. Many guesthouses offer a seventh night free, and you will have time to find the hidden coves, the best sunset bar and the bakery that sells out by nine every morning.

imagePairLeft.alt: Traveller in a yellow dress overlooking a tropical island bay

imagePairRight.alt: White-sand beach and palm-fringed villas on a tropical island

children.text: Plan one highlight a day
A boat trip, a market visit or a sunset dinner is plenty for one day. Leave the rest of your time open for swimming, reading under an umbrella and long lunches that stretch well into the afternoon.

Write a short wish list on the first evening, then choose one item each morning based on the weather and your mood. Some days that will be a snorkelling trip to a nearby reef, and on other days a simple walk along the sand is enough.

wideImage.alt: Wooden pier leading to overwater villas on clear lagoon water

children.text: Eat and live like a local
Ask your host where their own family eats. Fresh seafood, seasonal fruit and simple grilled dishes taste better in a small family-run restaurant, and the bill is usually a fraction of a resort menu.

Shop at the morning market for breakfast fruit, local cheese and fresh bread. Chatting with the stallholders is the easiest way to pick up a few words of the language and hear about festivals in town.
Coming home rested
A slow beach holiday rarely makes the busiest photo album, but it delivers what most of us need. You return home calm, well rested and already dreaming about going back next year.

blogs.title: Packing Smart: The Essential Carry-On Checklist for City Breaks
blogs.summary: Everything you need for a long weekend abroad, packed into one carry-on bag.

thumbnail.alt: Orange suitcase with a hat and passport in front of the Eiffel Tower

children.text: Why travel carry-on only

Skipping the checked bag saves time at both ends of your journey. You walk straight past the luggage belt, avoid surprise fees and never worry about lost suitcases. On a long weekend in a European city, one well-packed bag is all you need.
Build a capsule wardrobe
Two neutral colours so every top matches every pair of trousers
Five light tops, two bottoms and one smart jacket for evenings
One pair of comfortable walking shoes and one pair of sandals
A thin scarf that works as a wrap, pillow or beach towel
Keep documents together

Store your passport, boarding passes and insurance details in one slim pouch that lives in the same pocket every day. Save digital copies offline on your phone, so a flat battery or weak signal never leaves you stuck.

Add a small card with your hotel address written in the local language. Taxi drivers appreciate it, and it is the quickest way back after a long day of exploring when your phone has run out of charge.

imagePairLeft.alt: Woman in a yellow dress exploring an old town square

imagePairRight.alt: Traveller walking past colourful vegetable stalls at a street market

children.text: Master the liquids rule

Most airports still limit liquids to small bottles in a clear bag. Swap shampoo, soap and conditioner for solid bars, and buy sunscreen at your destination, which frees space and avoids spills in your bag.

Decant your favourite creams into tiny reusable pots and label each one clearly. Pack the clear bag last, right at the top of your carry-on, so you can lift it out in seconds at security and keep the queue behind you moving smoothly and quickly.

wideImage.alt: Colourful harbour village on the Italian coast

children.text: Leave room for souvenirs
Packing cubes compress clothing and keep your bag tidy, even after you repack it in a rush. Roll soft items instead of folding them, and fill your shoes with socks, chargers and other small things.
Aim to leave a quarter of your bag empty when you set off. That space soon fills with local coffee, a ceramic bowl from the market or a novel from a small secondhand bookshop.
Ready to go
With a simple checklist, packing for a city break takes less than an hour. Lay everything out the night before, remove one more item, zip up and enjoy the lighter journey ahead.

blogs.title: Island Hopping in Thailand: A Two-Week Route for First-Timers
blogs.summary: A relaxed two-week island route through the Andaman Sea, with ferry tips, where to stay and the best beaches on each stop.

thumbnail.alt: Wooden pier leading over turquoise water to a tropical island

children.text: Why the Andaman Sea

Thailand's west coast strings together limestone cliffs, quiet coves and easy ferry links, which makes it the perfect first island route. Two weeks gives you time to see four islands without rushing, and every stop has its own personality and pace.
What to book before you fly
Your first three nights in Ao Nang, close to the Krabi pier
Morning ferry seats between islands during the busy December peak
A speedboat transfer to Koh Lipe, which often sells out quickly
Travel insurance that covers boat trips, snorkelling and kayak tours
Start slow in Krabi

Spend three nights in Ao Nang to shake off the jet lag. Long-tail boats leave the beach every morning for Railay and the Hong Islands, so you can explore limestone lagoons and still be back for sunset.

On your last Krabi day, take the early boat to Railay before the crowds arrive. Walk the short trail to Phra Nang Cave beach, swim in the clear shallows and watch climbers tackle the towering cliffs above.

imagePairLeft.alt: Long-tail boats moored below a limestone rock in Krabi

imagePairRight.alt: Longtail boats below limestone cliffs on a turquoise Thai bay

children.text: Ferry routes that work
Ferries between the main islands run daily from November to April. Book the morning departures, when the sea is calmer, and you will arrive in time for lunch and an afternoon swim at your new beach.

Krabi to Koh Phi Phi takes about two hours, Phi Phi to Koh Lanta another ninety minutes, and the speedboat south to Koh Lipe around four hours. Keep valuables in a dry bag and grab a seat on the shaded side of the deck.

wideImage.alt: Wooden pier leading to overwater bungalows on a clear lagoon

children.text: Where to stay on each island
Choose small beachfront bungalows over big resorts. You will wake up a few steps from the water, pay less than at the chain hotels and support the local families who run them with real pride.
On Koh Lanta, pick the quieter south of the island for long empty beaches. On Koh Lipe, stay near Sunrise Beach so you can walk to the reef, the restaurants and the speedboat pier without a taxi.
Before you go
Pack reef-safe sunscreen, a light rain jacket and enough cash for the smaller islands, where ATMs are rare. Leave one free day on every island, because the best plans often happen there.

blogs.title: Chasing Waterfalls: Five Days on Iceland's Wild South Coast Road
blogs.summary: Plan a five-day drive along Iceland's Ring Road to see its most dramatic waterfalls, black sand beaches and glacier lagoons.

thumbnail.alt: Hiker in a red jacket facing a tall waterfall at sunset

children.text: Why drive the south coast

Iceland's south coast packs thundering waterfalls, black sand beaches and glacier lagoons into one easy stretch of the Ring Road. Five days lets you drive short distances, stop whenever the light is good and still reach Jokulsarlon before turning back west.
What to pack for the road
A fully waterproof jacket and trousers for the waterfall spray
Hiking boots with deep grip for wet rocks and gravel paths
Warm base layers, a hat and gloves, even in the summer
A reusable bottle, because the tap water is cold and excellent
Day one: the hidden falls
Pick up your rental car in Reykjavik and drive two hours east. Walk the muddy path behind Seljalandsfoss, where the curtain of water falls just a few metres in front of you, then dry off in the sun.

Follow the cliff path north for ten minutes to find Gljufrabui, a hidden waterfall tucked inside a narrow canyon. Wade through the shallow stream at the entrance and you will stand inside a cave of falling water.

imagePairLeft.alt: Skogafoss waterfall dropping from green cliffs onto a black gravel plain

imagePairRight.alt: Traveller with raised arms at a jungle waterfall

children.text: Day two: Skogafoss and Vik
Climb the 500 steps beside Skogafoss for a view over the river valley. Fit hikers can continue on the trail past more than twenty smaller waterfalls, each one tumbling through a deeper green gorge.

In the afternoon, drive to Reynisfjara to walk the black sand beach and see the basalt columns. Keep well back from the water, because sneaker waves arrive without warning, then spend a quiet night in the little village of Vik below the towering sea cliffs.

wideImage.alt: White car crossing a black lava plain below snow-capped mountains in Iceland

children.text: Planning the rest of your route

Spend day three at Fjadrargljufur canyon and the moss-covered lava fields near Kirkjubaejarklaustur. Book a guided glacier hike at Skaftafell for day four, since walking on the ice alone is never safe.
On day five, reach Jokulsarlon early to watch icebergs drift out to sea, then cross the road to Diamond Beach. Allow a full day for the five-hour drive back to Reykjavik with plenty of stops.
Best time to visit
June to August brings near-endless daylight and open mountain roads. September offers fewer crowds, autumn colours and the first real chance of seeing the northern lights dancing over the coast.

blogs.title: Planning Your First Trip Together Without Stress or Arguments
blogs.summary: Simple ways for couples and friends to agree on a budget, share the planning and enjoy every day of their first trip together.

thumbnail.alt: Smiling couple with backpacks reading a map in a forest

children.text: Start with a shared vision

Before anyone opens a booking site, sit down together and describe your perfect day away. One of you may picture lazy beach mornings, the other busy city streets. Finding the overlap early saves hours of debate and makes every later decision easier.
Split the planning fairly
One person books the flights, airport transfers and travel insurance
The other researches stays, neighbourhoods and the best local cafes
Choose the restaurants, day trips and evening plans together each week
Keep every booking and receipt in one shared online folder
Agree on the budget first

Talk about money before you talk about destinations. Set a daily amount for food, transport and activities, and agree how you will split shared costs, so nobody has to keep score while you are away on holiday.

Leave a little room in the budget for surprises. A spontaneous boat trip or a special dinner can become the best memory of the holiday, and it feels far better when it fits the plan you made together.

imagePairLeft.alt: Two hikers smiling on a mountain trail

imagePairRight.alt: Couple reading a paper map together on a sunny street

children.text: Each person picks one must-do
Let each traveller choose one experience that is not up for debate. A cooking class, a sunrise hike or a day at the spa gives everyone something personal to look forward to during the trip.

Put both choices in the calendar first and plan the rest of the days around them. When the trip includes something each of you truly wanted, the smaller compromises feel easy, and you will find it simpler to say yes to new ideas along the way.

wideImage.alt: Two hikers on a rocky lookout above an island-dotted bay

children.text: Keep the days relaxed
Back-to-back sightseeing tires everyone out, even the most energetic traveller. Plan a free afternoon every few days to rest, wander without a map or simply sit in a cafe and watch the city go by.
Expect at least one thing to go wrong, from a late train to a rainy beach day. Agree to laugh it off, find a backup plan together and never let small delays spoil a whole day.
Final thoughts
The best first trips are not the most planned ones. They are the ones where both of you feel heard, share the small decisions and come home talking about the next adventure.

Designed for travellers who want culture without the rush, every day pairs a guided morning with a free afternoon. Use the spare hours for hidden tea houses, a pottery class near Kiyomizu-dera and slow evening walks along the Kamo River as the city lights up.

Built for travellers who would rather linger than rush, each day mixes one guided outing with free time by the sea. Spend the spare hours swimming from the rocks, browsing ceramic shops in Vietri or sipping limoncello on a terrace as the bells ring out.

Planned for walkers of every level, mornings bring a guided hike or rail excursion and afternoons stay free. Use the extra time to paddle in Bachalpsee, visit a cheese dairy above Lauterbrunnen or simply sit on your balcony with a view of thundering waterfalls.

Built for wildlife lovers who also want comfort, days start early with a game drive and slow down in the afternoon heat. Spend the quiet hours by the lodge pool, visiting a Maasai village with a local host or sketching the plains from your veranda.

Planned for travellers who want paradise at an easy pace, every day offers one guided outing and long hours on the sand. Fill the gaps with snorkelling in calm lagoons, a Creole cooking lesson with a local family or a sunset walk at Anse Lazio.

destinations.name: Kyoto
destinations.tagline: Temples, tea houses and maple valleys
destinations.summary: Walk lantern-lit lanes, sip matcha in quiet tea houses and watch maple valleys turn red in Kyoto, the old imperial capital and cultural heart of Japan.
destinations.heroText: Discover temples, tea houses and maple valleys in Japan's old capital, from moss gardens to lively food markets

cardImage.alt: Vermilion shrine gate in Kyoto on a clear morning

children.text: Kyoto was Japan's capital for over a thousand years, and its old soul still shows on every street. Wooden townhouses, raked stone gardens and more than 1,600 temples sit between modern avenues, so one short walk can lead from a busy market to a silent moss garden with a trickling bamboo water spout. Come for the culture, the crafts and the seasonal food, then stay for the slow, lantern-lit evenings in the old Gion district.
See the vermilion torii gates of Fushimi Inari before the morning crowds arrive
Stay in a family-run ryokan with tatami rooms, kimono robes and a hot spring bath
Taste seasonal kaiseki dinners, matcha sweets and street snacks in Nishiki Market
Catch soft cherry blossom in spring or fiery red maple valleys in late autumn
Walk the Arashiyama bamboo grove at sunrise, well before the tour buses arrive.
Join a tea ceremony led by a local master in a historic tea house.
Explore the geisha district of Gion along lantern-lit Hanamikoji Street.
See the golden Kinkaku-ji pavilion reflected in its mirror pond.

Our Kyoto planners live in the Kansai region and book small, family-run ryokans that rarely appear on big booking sites. Every tour starts early to beat the crowds at the famous temples, while afternoons stay free so you can wander the old lanes at your own pace.

You also get a pocket Wi-Fi, a preloaded IC travel card and an English-speaking contact on call for the whole trip. If plans change, we rebook trains, guides and restaurant tables for you, so a rainy day becomes a museum and tea house day instead of a lost one in the city.
Stays range from boutique ryokans in Gion to modern city hotels
Buses and the subway reach every major sight across the whole city
Many temples close by 5 pm, so plan the famous gardens for mornings
Most visitors from the US, UK and EU need no visa for short trips
Nara and its friendly deer are an easy day trip, 45 minutes by train

destinations.name: Amalfi Coast
destinations.summary: Pastel villages stacked on sea cliffs, lemon groves, boat days to Capri and long seafood lunches make the Amalfi Coast Italy's most romantic shoreline.
destinations.heroText: Explore pastel cliff villages, lemon groves and hidden coves, from Capri boat days to long seaside lunches in Italy

cardImage.alt: Colourful harbour village on the Italian coast

children.text: South of Naples, the Amalfi Coast winds for fifty kilometres between steep green mountains and a deep blue sea. Positano, Amalfi and Ravello cling to the cliffs in shades of peach and lemon, linked by one dramatic coastal road and a fleet of small, busy ferries. Days here are about wide sea views, morning swims in clear coves and long dinners that last until the village lights come on above the harbour.
Swim in quiet turquoise coves that you can only reach by a private wooden boat
Hike the Path of the Gods trail high above the sea and the terraced lemon groves
Eat fresh pasta, creamy mozzarella and lemon desserts at family-run trattorias
Base yourself in a garden hotel with a sunny terrace hanging over the blue water
Spend a private boat day around Capri and the famous Faraglioni sea rocks.
Walk the Path of the Gods from the hills of Bomerano down to Positano.
Take a hands-on pasta and pizza cooking class in a Ravello villa garden.
Taste homemade limoncello at a family lemon farm above Amalfi.

Summer on the coast books out months ahead, so our local partners hold rooms in small sea-view hotels and reserve ferry and boat slots for you. That means no long queues at the busy piers and no endless searching for a free table at sunset on a warm July evening.

Private transfers from Naples airport are included, which saves you the famous traffic jams on the coast road. Our team also books beach club loungers, guided hikes and dinner tables, and a local host is a phone call away if the sea turns rough and a boat day needs to move.
Hotels range from family-run B&Bs to clifftop luxury retreats by the sea
Ferries are the easiest way to travel between villages in summer
Expect many steps, so pack light walking shoes and a small daypack
Beach clubs and loungers need booking well ahead in July and August
Pompeii and Naples are both easy day trips from the coast

destinations.name: Swiss Alps
destinations.summary: Ride cogwheel trains to glacier viewpoints, hike flower meadows below the Eiger and sleep in wooden chalets in the classic villages of the Swiss Alps.
destinations.heroText: Discover chalet villages, glaciers and scenic trains, from flower meadows to sunrise views of the famous Matterhorn

cardImage.alt: Snow-capped Swiss Alps above a green valley

children.text: The Swiss Alps pack glaciers, turquoise lakes and car-free villages into a small, beautifully connected area. Trains, boats and cable cars run like clockwork, so you can wake in a Grindelwald chalet, lunch by the shore of Lake Brienz and still catch sunset from a mountain terrace. Summer brings wildflowers and easy hikes, while winter turns every snowy slope into a lively ski and sledging playground.
Ride the train up to the Jungfraujoch, the highest railway station in Europe
Walk gentle trails past wildflower meadows, wooden barns and grazing dairy cows
Travel everywhere by scenic train, boat and bus with a single Swiss Travel Pass
Warm up with cheese fondue and warm raclette in cosy family-run mountain chalets
Ride the cogwheel railway up to the vast Aletsch glacier viewpoint at the top.
Cross the First cliff walk, then hike up to the calm Bachalpsee lake.
Cruise across the turquoise Lake Brienz to the roaring Giessbach waterfalls.
Watch the Matterhorn turn pink at sunrise above Zermatt village.

We plan your route around the mountain weather, so high excursions stay flexible and move to clear days at no extra cost. Your luggage travels ahead between villages by train, which means you only carry a light day pack as you hike from one green valley to the next.

Every trip includes a Swiss Travel Pass and chalet stays chosen by our Alpine specialists, who have walked every trail they suggest. You also get a local contact on call, mountain lift tickets booked in advance and restaurant tips for the best rosti and fondue in each village.
Stays range from wooden chalets to grand old lakeside hotels in town
The Swiss Travel Pass covers most trains, boats and city buses
Mountain weather changes fast, so pack warm layers and a jacket
Cards are accepted almost everywhere, even in the small villages
Lucerne and Bern are easy day trips from Interlaken by train

destinations.name: Lofoten Islands
destinations.tagline: Fjords, fishing cabins and midnight sun
destinations.summary: Granite peaks rise straight from the sea in Arctic Norway. Sleep in red fishing cabins, hike ridge trails and kayak empty beaches in the Lofoten Islands.
destinations.heroText: Explore Arctic fjords, red fishing cabins and granite peaks, from midnight sun hikes to northern lights nights

cardImage.alt: Red fishing cabins below granite peaks in Lofoten

children.text: Above the Arctic Circle, the Lofoten Islands look like a mountain range that sank into the sea. Bright red fishing cabins sit on stilts below sharp granite peaks, and white sandy beaches glow turquoise on clear days. Summer brings the midnight sun and long ridge hikes, while late winter brings snowy summits, quiet empty roads and green northern lights dancing over the deep, silent fjords at night.
Sleep in a traditional red rorbu fishing cabin right on the water's edge
Hike ridge trails with wide views over fjords, white beaches and fishing villages
See the endless midnight sun in summer or the green northern lights in late winter
Eat the freshest cod, Arctic char and creamy fish soup you will find in Norway
Climb the stone steps of Reinebringen for the classic view over Reine village.
Kayak calm fjord water past sea eagles, seals and empty sandy bays.
Take a small local ferry across the fjord to the white sands of Bunes beach.
Warm up in a waterside sauna, then take a quick dip in the Arctic sea.

Cabins in the best villages sell out early, and Arctic weather changes by the hour. Our Norway team books seafront rorbu stays months ahead and keeps each day flexible, so hikes, boat trips and photo stops always move to the clearest skies of your week in the islands.

A rental car and a local host on call are included, giving you freedom on the islands with real support close by. We also share offline maps, tide times and an aurora forecast guide, and we rebook ferries or tours for you if a big storm rolls in from the open Norwegian Sea.
Stays range from simple rorbu cabins to design hotels by the sea
A car is the best way to drive the scenic E10 road between islands
Pack warm layers and a windproof jacket, even in the middle of summer
Shops and cafes in small villages keep short opening hours
Henningsvaer and Nusfjord make easy, scenic day trips by car

destinations.name: Thai Islands
destinations.summary: Hop between limestone islands by longtail boat, snorkel hidden lagoons and unwind in beach villas along the Andaman coast of the Thai Islands.
destinations.heroText: Discover limestone bays, coral reefs and beach villas, from longtail boat days to lively Thai night markets by the sea

cardImage.alt: Longtail boats below limestone cliffs on a turquoise Thai bay

children.text: Along Thailand's Andaman coast, hundreds of limestone islands rise from water so clear you can see the reef from the boat. Krabi, Koh Lanta and the Phi Phi islands mix lively night markets with quiet sandy beaches, and every evening ends with a sunset that turns the tall cliffs gold. It is easy, warm and friendly, made for slow island days, long swims and fresh seafood dinners on the beach at dusk.
Island hop by private longtail boat to hidden lagoons and empty white beaches
Snorkel colourful coral reefs full of tropical fish, rays and gentle sea turtles
Stay in quiet beachfront villas with hammocks strung right over the soft white sand
Eat fresh Thai curries and grilled seafood at busy, colourful night markets
Swim in the emerald Hong lagoon at dawn, well before the busy day boats arrive.
Kayak through the quiet sea caves and green mangroves of Phang Nga Bay.
Learn to cook a fragrant green curry in a family kitchen garden on Koh Lanta.
Watch the sunset from Railay beach between towering cliffs.

Our Thailand team times every boat trip with the tides and leaves early, so you reach the famous bays while they are still calm and quiet. Ferries, transfers and island hotels are all linked up for you, with no long waits at busy piers or crowded ticket desks.

Each trip includes reef-safe snorkel gear, travel insurance advice and round-the-clock local support in English. We also pick villas with shade, good beds and fast Wi-Fi, and we can add a cooking class, a Thai massage or a private sunset cruise on any day of your island holiday.
Stays range from bamboo beach bungalows to private pool villas
Ferries and longtail boats connect all of the main Andaman islands
May to October brings rain and rougher seas on the Andaman coast
Cover your shoulders and knees when you visit the island temples
Phi Phi and the Hong islands are easy day trips from Krabi town

destinations.name: Bali
destinations.summary: Green rice terraces, sea temples, surf breaks and private pool villas make Bali the perfect island for honeymoons, wellness escapes and slow travel.
destinations.heroText: Explore rice terraces, sea temples and surf beaches, from jungle pool villas to the golden sunset cliffs of Uluwatu

cardImage.alt: Wooden pier leading to overwater villas on clear lagoon water

children.text: Bali is an island of daily offerings, temple ceremonies and emerald rice terraces. Ubud is its creative green heart, full of yoga studios, craft markets and jungle villas, while the south coast brings surf beaches and clifftop sunsets at Uluwatu. Wherever you stay, the warmth of Balinese hospitality makes every day feel easy, slow and quietly special from the very first morning to the last evening.
Walk the Tegallalang rice terraces in the soft golden light of early dawn
Stay in a private pool villa surrounded by tall palms and lush green jungle views
Join a traditional water blessing ceremony at the sacred spring temple of Tirta Empul
Surf, swim or simply unwind on the wide golden sandy beaches of the south coast
Explore the emerald landscapes of Ubud and experience authentic Balinese culture.
Relax in beach resorts with crystal-clear water and golden sunsets.
Visit Tanah Lot and Uluwatu Temple perched dramatically over the ocean.
Ride world-class waves and soak up Bali's laid-back surf culture.

Our Bali planners hand-pick villas with private pools and real privacy, away from the busy streets of the south. Drivers, temple guides and spa rituals are all arranged before you land, so the only plan you need to make each morning is when to take your first swim.

Honeymoon and wellness extras, like floating breakfasts, flower baths and sunrise yoga, can be added to any trip. You also get a local SIM card, an English-speaking host on call and a driver who knows the quiet back roads, so you skip the traffic and see the island's calmest corners.
Stays range from jungle villas in Ubud to clifftop beach resorts
A private driver is the easiest way to get around the whole island
Bring a sarong for temple visits, or borrow one at the temple gate
The rainy season usually runs from early November to late March
The Nusa islands are a short speedboat ride away from Sanur
